items.title: Enzymes can accelerate reactions by a factor of 10 to the 17
items.claim: Orotidine monophosphate decarboxylase (OMP decarboxylase) without an enzyme has a half-life of about 78 million years. The enzyme cuts the half-life to 18 milliseconds — an acceleration factor of 1.4 times 10 to the 17.
items.prompt: How is such an enormous rate enhancement physically possible?

options.text: Enzymes add energy to the molecules

Enzymes lower the activation energy by positioning substrates precisely, stabilising the transition state, and excluding water from the reaction site — small lowering of Ea gives exponential acceleration because rate scales as exp(-Ea/RT)
Enzymes use radiation to speed reactions

items.reveal:
From Arrhenius: k = A exp(-Ea/RT). Lower Ea by just 100 kJ/mol at body temperature and the rate goes up by exp(100,000/2479) ≈ 10 to the 17.

Enzymes don't change the equilibrium — they speed approach to it. They orient substrates, exclude bulk water, and bind the transition state more tightly than they bind the substrate. Linus Pauling proposed this 'transition-state binding' picture in 1948.

Designing catalysts that achieve enzyme-level rate enhancements remains a frontier challenge. AI-assisted enzyme design (David Baker's lab, 2020s) is closing the gap.
items.why: Catalysts are taught as 'providing an alternative pathway'. The exponential rate-law sensitivity means even small Ea changes give huge rate changes.

items.title: A mole of marshmallows would cover the USA 600 miles deep
items.claim: 6.022 times 10 to the 23 is just a number until you try to picture it. Avogadro's number of marshmallows would bury the entire surface of the United States to a depth of 600 miles.
items.prompt: Roughly how many moles of water molecules are in a single drop (about 0.05 mL)?

options.text: About 0.003 moles, which is roughly 1.7 times 10 to the 21 molecules
Around 6 times 10 to the 23 — one drop is one mole
About 0.05 moles, the same as the volume in millilitres

items.reveal_title: Even a microscopic drop contains stupefying numbers of molecules
items.reveal:
0.05 mL of water has a mass of 0.05 g. Water is 18 g per mole, so 0.05 / 18 equals about 0.0028 mol. Multiply by Avogadro's number and you get roughly 1.7 times 10 to the 21 molecules.

If you counted those molecules at one per second, it would take about 50 trillion years — over 3000 times the age of the universe. Chemistry is the study of mind-bending counts of incredibly tiny things.
items.why: The mole is treated as a unit conversion when it should be treated as a stark statement about scale.

items.title: Frost forms by water vapour skipping the liquid state entirely
items.claim: Water vapour in cold air can deposit directly onto a windowpane as ice crystals without ever becoming liquid. The reverse — solid to gas without melting — is called sublimation, and is how freeze-drying works.
items.prompt: Why does water sometimes skip the liquid stage?

options.text: Water bends the laws of phase transitions
At pressures below the triple point (6.1 mbar for water) the liquid phase is not stable — water can only exist as solid or vapour, and transitions go directly between them
Frost forms only from existing ice
Liquid water is too dense for cold air

items.reveal_title: Below the triple point, liquid disappears
items.reveal:
Water's triple point sits at 0.01°C and 6.1 millibar — the only temperature and pressure where solid, liquid and vapour coexist. Below this pressure the liquid phase is unstable; water can only be vapour or ice, and crossing the boundary means sublimation or deposition.

At atmospheric pressure (1013 mbar) water can be liquid between 0 and 100°C, but small pockets of supercooled vapour near a cold surface can deposit straight to solid because the local equilibrium prefers ice over the metastable liquid intermediate.

Freeze-drying exploits this: freeze food, lower the pressure below the triple point, and the ice sublimes away with no melting. The structure is preserved, water is removed, and the result is light, stable food (instant coffee, astronaut meals, pharmaceutical formulations).
items.why: Solid to gas skipping liquid is treated as a curiosity. It is the dominant transition at low pressure and underpins multibillion-dollar industries.
